chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Jameel ibn Darraj, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The days of Al-Adha are two days after the day of sacrifice, and one day in the provinces (cities).

key_terms.يَوْمِ النَّحْرِ: The day of sacrifice (12th Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: How many days are the days of Eid al-Adha in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi delineates the specific duration of the Days of Tashriq for animal sacrifice, distinguishing between the sacred precincts of Mecca and other regions. It reflects the Shia jurisprudential view that the permissibility of sacrificing and eating the meat is limited to three days in Mecca (including the Day of Naḥr) and only one day elsewhere, a nuance derived from the interplay of Quranic verses and Prophetic practice.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The (Eid) Al-Azha is two days after the day of the sacrifice, and one day in the cities’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Jamil ibn Darraj from Muhammad ibn Muslim who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, ‘has said,
‘Al-Adha’ is for two days after the day of al-Nahr (slaughtering the offering on 10th of Dhu al-Hajjah) and it is one day in the cities/”NOTE: Fatwa best explains Hadith 1-2 of this Chapter.
